runs.name: Universal Health Services, Inc.; no rename, merger, spin-off or split in the 8-Ks since 2026-03; Talkspace acquired 2026-08; four share classes
runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q1; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$178.90** a Class B share (quote of 2026-10-13 through `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **58,936,515**, four classes counted alike (Class A 6,574,600, B 51,687,770, C 661,688, D 12,457; 10-Q cover at 2026-07-31, `0001193125-26-340278`; `cover_shares.py` the same; repurchased shares retired, no treasury line; the August 2026 424B5s and 8-Ks carry no newer count); cap **$10,544M**; net debt **$5,699M** ($4,713M at 2026-06-30 plus the Talkspace financing net of its cash and the Ireland purchase, both after the quarter; operating leases left out). Sovereign **5.60%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-09). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (`0001193125-26-071676`), 10-Ks FY2024, FY2023, FY2021, FY2019 and FY2016, 10-Q to 2026-06-30, proxy 2026 (`0001193125-26-148814`), the 8-Ks of 2026-08-13, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-21; one figure cross-checked (FY2025 operating cash $1,864.4M against the filed statement). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the FY2025 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. Competitors: the 10-K names rivals by kind only, none by name; the analyst took HCA, CYH and ACHC as a CONVENTION of the run (Tenet left out because its commit subjects were seen). **Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: behavioral health 62% of 2021 to 2025 segment pretax income ($5,906M against acute $3,592M), so it decides; state Medicaid supplemental payments net of provider taxes $1,339M in 2025, 68% of pretax income of $1,972M, against $161M in 2016, pretax income without the layer $995M (2016) and $689M (2025) while revenue rose from $9,766M to $17,365M; most programs approved year to year; the filer writes one number for the OBBBA cut ($432M to $480M by 2032 in the 10-K, about $500M in the 10-Q, "subject to change, potentially by material amounts") and declines to estimate the January 2026 CMS provider-tax rule, the eligibility rules and the Managed Care Rule; behavioral health 42% Medicaid; NATURE because the filer itself declines the deciding forecast; the counter-case written out because of a declared anchor. Q2 to Q12 not reached. After the stop: pre-interest pretax margin 2016 to 2025 HCA 15.4%, UHS 10.8%, ACHC 6.1%, CYH 4.5%, UHS below HCA every year; goodwill flat ($3,784M to $3,990M); equity $4,533M to $7,276M while shares fell from about 97M to about 64M; self-insured liability $449M; buybacks at average prices of $193.38 (2025), $228.30 (2025 Q4) and $169.43 (2026 Q2), no expiration and no price named, above the bottom of the computed range. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: window 2021 to 2025 with the CARES Act repayments added back to the years paid (specific (a)), the literal window beside; all capital spending charged (no maintenance split filed); not a serial acquirer; owner cash all-equity average $724M, growth 3.31%; range **$122.54 to $188.49 a share all-equity** against $178.90; no case earns the floor (4.45% to 5.78%); fair **$41.66 all-equity, $101.80 equity-only**, computation only; the analyst's own labelled sensitivity with the filer's OBBBA estimate deducted, $23.70 to $89.66, not part of the figures; no alert (box not OUT at Q7 or IN). Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the $127M False Claims Act settlement of 2020 with a corporate integrity agreement; the Cumberland verdict and some forty more plaintiffs; a $500M Nevada punitive award the company expects cut to about $14M; liability cover excluding sexual abuse incidents from March 2025; the founder, Executive Chairman, with 88.9% of the general voting power. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing filtered on the ticker before the blind rule was read closely showed one file name, a 2026-07-15 UHS run, not opened (the self-audit box left unchecked for it); the session's git snapshot showed the THC fold's commit subjects; none used. Commits 2782a247, e7ad2aa2. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for UHS or Universal Health). Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` passed; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_fragcheck.py` 15 quoted cites, no slip, no missing id, no E-id. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) the parts test cannot be run cleanly when the decisive variable is reported only for the whole (the supplemental layer is consolidated only), and the text does not say whether it is judged at the whole or at the part; (2) Q1's test 5 has no rule for a partial, caveated insider forecast, so a second analyst could pass Q1 on the written OBBBA number (the THC and CYH runs of the same day reported the near gap of a government-set price as the key variable); (3) Q7's growth specifics give no place for a decline the filer itself quantifies; (4) the convention does not say whether a subsequent acquisition's own cash is netted against its financing. Could not get: the segment split of the supplemental layer, a maintenance split of capital spending, a share count after 2026-07-31, the revolver draw for Talkspace.
runs.narr: Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE): the acute and behavioral hospital company whose deciding part, behavioral health (62% of five-year segment pretax income, 42% Medicaid), shares a state Medicaid supplemental layer of $1,339M, 68% of 2025 pretax income and $161M in 2016, approved year to year and cut by a 2025 law whose full effect the filer declines to estimate beyond one caveated number. After the stop: pre-interest pretax margin 10.8% over ten years against HCA 15.4%, below it every year; buybacks at $169 to $228 with no price named. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range $122.54 to $188.49 a share all-equity against $178.90, no case earns the floor, fair $41.66 all-equity, $101.80 equity-only. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the 2020 $127M False Claims Act settlement, the Cumberland and Nevada verdicts, the founder's 88.9% of the vote.
